name: Valleys
overview: The valleys in Scripture often serve as significant locations for both conflict and provision. For example, the vale of Siddim was the site of a fierce battle involving multiple kings (Genesis 14:3, 8), while the valley of Shaveh was a place of royal encounter and peace (Genesis 14:17). Valleys also represent places of dwelling and movement, as seen when Isaac pitched his tent in the valley of Gerar (Genesis 26:17) and when the Israelites camped in the valley of Zared during their journey (Numbers 21:12). These passages highlight valleys as settings where God's people experience both trials and divine sustenance.
